name: THE CLAIMS REGISTRAR
materialIdentity: Pale institutional wood, paper and dust (17b), pulled to mid value so it separates from the map screen it is entered from
note: Doc 05 Room 7, with THE TWO LINES replaced by errata doc 19 section 2. The contradiction doc 19 settles: THE TWO LINES needed two occupied queues and THE NUMBER SPINDLE says there is one other man in the room. The spindle survives -- ticket ninety-one in a room containing two people is the funnier and more particular joke -- and the queues are rewritten empty, which also costs no drawn crowd. TWO THINGS ARE PROVISIONAL AND MARKED AS SUCH. The rects are placed against doc 12's prompt and not against art, because the room is not composed; they are the one part of this file that must be re-sited when it is. And five of doc 05's ten hotspots -- THE LEDGER, THE COUNTER, THE BENCH, THE MAP OF CLAIMS, SUMP'S PEN -- are marked '(working script)' there and are absent here rather than invented. Doc 20 answers the question this file used to leave open: it is reached from the town map, declared in `entrances` above. Lines EXTRACTED from docs/25-rooms-05-07.md by tools/extract-content.mjs. Do not edit: change doc 25 and re-run.

entrances.note: Doc 20's graph: Room 7 is reached from the town map, not from a facade on Main Street. The map screen is Room 0 and is not built, so this states a route to a room that does not exist yet -- which doc 20 rule 1 asks for and check-room-entries reports as pending rather than failing. The id is provisional until the map screen picks one.

LOOK_AT.say: A bench along the wall for those waiting. It seats nine.
repeat: The seat is worn at one end only. Everybody sits nearest the window.
I have sat on it. It is a bench and it is doing what it can.
Nothing.
Nothing. There is nobody on it.

LOOK_AT.say: The claims ledger. Every filing in the district, in one book, in one hand.
repeat: Claim One is on the first page and it is one line long.
Six thousand entries after it, and all six thousand are looking for the first one.
Nothing.
Nothing. It has the whole town in it and no opinion about any of it.

LOOK_AT.say: A pen, chained to the counter. The chain is longer than the counter requires.
repeat: It has been chained since before the chain was needed, or since somebody proved it was.
It writes. I have used it. It is a perfectly good pen on a chain.
Nothing.
Nothing.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is chained. That is the entire design.

LOOK_AT.say: A counter built a little too high to lean on comfortably. I have tested this.
repeat: Worn in a band where four thousand men have rested their forearms and been told to wait.
There is a brass rail along the front. Somebody once expected a crowd.
Nothing.
Nothing.

LOOK_AT.say: Forms in triplicate, and a sign explaining that the third copy is for the applicant. There is no third copy in any of the slots.
repeat: Twelve slots. The third-copy slot is empty in all twelve.
I have taken one of each. It seemed prudent and it was not.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper, settling. It is a sound like a very slow argument.
repeat: Paper, settling.
Nothing.

overrides.PICK_UP: I have taken one of each already and it did not help.

LOOK_AT.say: Every claim in the district, pinned and numbered. Claim One is a rectangle like all the others.
repeat: There is no cross on it. I had expected a cross.
Somebody has put a pin in it and taken the pin out again. There is a hole.
Nothing.
Nothing.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is pinned to the wall, and it is the only accurate map in town.

hotspots.name: THE NUMBER SPINDLE
hotspots.note: Doc 19 section 2: this is the hotspot the contradiction was settled in favour of.

LOOK_AT.say: A spindle of numbered tickets. I am ninety-one. There is one other man in the room and he is forty.
repeat: Ninety-one. The other man is still forty.
I have taken ninety-two, to see. Nobody stopped me.
Nothing.
Nothing. It waits extremely well.

overrides.PICK_UP: I have my ticket. Taking the spindle would be a different sort of crime.

LOOK_AT.say: A door, locked, with a statute posted beside it explaining precisely who may pass through. I am not among them.
repeat: The statute beside it lists four persons who may pass. I am none of them, and neither is Mr Sump.
Still locked. It is very consistently locked.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is very thick and there is nothing behind it that moves.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all. Whatever is in there is not moving.

overrides.OPEN: Locked. It is the only locked door in Consolation.
overrides.PULL: Locked, and it does not give at all.

LOOK_AT.say: The office clock. It is authoritative and it is wrong.
repeat: Eleven minutes fast, and authoritative about it.
It is the only clock in Consolation that anybody obeys.

LISTEN_TO.say: Running eleven minutes fast, which I know because I own a watch that agrees with it and I do not trust that either.
repeat: Ticking. Fast.
Ticking. I have stopped hearing it, which took four days.

overrides.USE: I am not adjusting the Registrar's clock.

hotspots.name: THE TWO LINES
hotspots.note: Errata doc 19 section 2, verbatim. Rewritten under ruling 19b so the joke needs no drawn crowd.

LOOK_AT.say: Two roped lines, two signs. FILING and INQUIRIES. There is nobody in either of them and the ropes are up regardless.
repeat: The ropes have been up long enough to have worn the paint off the posts.
I have stood in both, to be certain. It made no difference to anything.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Two empty queues are quieter than one.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all. There is a clock, and there is a man, and that is the whole of it.

exits.name: THE STREET DOOR
exits.note: Doc 20 reaches Room 7 through the town map, so this is the way back rather than the way in -- and doc 25 writes it, which is why it exists now.

LOOK_AT.say: The door out. It has a bell on a spring that announces everyone.
repeat: The bell has announced me four times today.
Mr Sump has not looked up at that bell in some years, I should think.
The street.
The bell, faintly, still settling.
